To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The gravity-driven growth of active folds in the deep Niger Delta has influenced channel morphology and sedimentary processes in four submarine channel systems.

(1) modern channels are actively evolving in response to the active growth of folds and thrusts in the toe of deep-water Niger Delta, (2) these channels are responding to actively growing structures by adjusting their width, depth, and slope, and (3) the channels are responding to these actively growing structures by migrating and adjusting their sinuosity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the interaction between submarine channels with actively growing folds and fault-bend folds, and how the resulting morphodynamic processes have influenced the evolution of the deep-water Niger delta.
